prompt: A writer works hard on a problem scene for an hour with no progress, takes a walk, and an idea arrives. Which claim about this is most careful and accurate?

options.text: Breaks magically solve problems with no prior effort needed
Walking always produces ideas within ten minutes
A break after sustained effort can help — stepping away sometimes allows a fresh approach — but it follows the work rather than replacing it
The idea proves effort was unnecessary all along

explanation: Incubation effects are modest and depend on having first engaged seriously with the problem. The walk helped after effortful work; it is not a substitute for that work or a guaranteed fix.
